answer: The lengthsman reads the water level of every pound each morning, and the book holds the level beside the rainfall for the day. A echo pound claimed as read fails the book: the gauge must have been read at the gale of the morning, and a pound never read has no level to file. Buying a false water record costs 10,100 in bribes to the lengthsman and a forged gauge, and the jetty book is compared with the feeder reservoir's own figures, so a level whose reading was never entered is found out by the dry pound.
